In brief: our current warm and humid weather pattern looks set to continue for the rest of the week, with temperatures likely to push into the mid-30s by tomorrow. While we're not expecting any significant rain events just yet, there are some hints of increased moisture in the atmosphere that could lead to some showers later in the week. For now, though, it's looking like a pretty typical late April week in Abuja, with plenty of sunshine and just a few clouds drifting lazily across the sky.

As we take a look at the current conditions, it's clear that the heat is already starting to build. With a temperature of 24°C and a feels-like temperature of 28°C, it's no surprise that many of us are already reaching for the air conditioner or a cool drink. The humidity is also relatively high, at 84%, which is helping to make the air feel even warmer. Out on the roads, the Nnamdi Azikiwe Expressway is looking good, with traffic moving at a decent pace and no major congestion to report. If you're planning on heading out to the National Assembly or the National Mosque, you shouldn't have too much trouble getting there.

One of the key factors in our weather pattern this week is the wind. Or, rather, the lack thereof. With a wind speed of just 3 km/h, it's clear that the atmosphere is pretty stagnant at the moment. This can help to trap heat and moisture close to the surface, making the air feel warmer and more oppressive. As we look ahead to the rest of the week, it's possible that we could see some changes in the wind pattern, which could help to bring some relief from the heat.

### Current Weather Pattern
The current weather pattern is dominated by high pressure, which is helping to keep the skies clear and the sun shining. This high pressure is also helping to suppress the formation of clouds and precipitation, which is why we're not seeing much in the way of rain at the moment. As we look ahead to the rest of the week, it's possible that this high pressure could start to break down, allowing some moisture to move into the area.

As we head into the next few days, it's looking like the heat will continue to build. We're expecting to see temperatures push into the mid-30s, possibly even touching 35°C by tomorrow. This is pretty typical for this time of year, but it's still worth taking some precautions to stay cool. Make sure to stay hydrated, wear light and loose-fitting clothing, and try to stay out of the sun during the hottest part of the day. If you're planning on heading out to the Millennium Park or the Abuja National Park, be sure to bring plenty of water and take regular breaks in the shade.

As we look ahead to the rest of the week, it's possible that we could see some changes in the wind pattern, which could help to bring some relief from the heat.
